setup: You changed the agreed order of work without asking Michel. At this morning's meeting he turns to you.
opening: That's not what we agreed. You always change the plan at the last minute.

acknowledge.line: I need to know what changed and how we will avoid another last-minute change.

endings.acknowledge: OK. If you check with me first, I can live with changes. Let's write that down.
endings.defend: Then nothing will change, and I'll keep redoing my work.
endings.attack: I asked a fair question. I'll take this to the team lead.
endings.withdraw: So we're leaving it. Then it'll happen again next month.

acknowledge.debrief: Accepting your part helps you and Michel agree what to do next.

defend.line: I hear your reasons, but I still had to redo my work. What will you do differently?

endings.acknowledge: Thank you. That's what I needed. Let's look at the new order together.
endings.defend: Then this will keep happening, and I'll keep paying for it.
endings.attack: A few hours of my work. I'm done with this conversation.

defend.debrief: Blaming someone else doesn't resolve Michel's extra work.

attack.line: I'm trying to talk about the plan. Can we discuss that without attacking each other?

endings.acknowledge: Thank you. Then let's agree how changes work from now on.
endings.defend: It didn't sound like facts to me. Let's leave it for now.
endings.attack: I'm not doing this. Talk to me when you can be civil.
endings.withdraw: Then I'll raise it with the team lead.

attack.debrief: Attacking Michel makes it harder to agree on the plan.

withdraw.line: We still need to resolve the plan. Are you willing to come back to this conversation?

endings.acknowledge: Thank you. Let's start with what's left of my part.
endings.defend: I redid hours of work. I'm not letting this go.
endings.attack: I asked a simple question. I'll take this to the team lead.

withdraw.debrief: Ending the discussion without agreeing to return leaves the problem unresolved.

pause.line: All right. Let's take ten minutes and come back to agree on the plan.

endings.acknowledge: Thanks. That's what I needed to hear. Let's fix the new order together.
endings.withdraw: You said we'd come back to this. Leaving it is exactly the problem.
endings.pause: Tomorrow at nine, then. I'll hold you to it.

pause.debrief: Agreeing when to return gives you time to think without ending the discussion.

opening.acknowledge: You're right, I changed it late and didn't check with you first. I can see why that's frustrating.
opening.defend: That's not fair. The client changed their mind, not me. I had no choice.
opening.attack: Here we go again. Maybe if you read your emails you'd have known.
opening.withdraw: OK. Never mind. Let's move on to the next item.
opening.pause: I want to answer this properly. Can we take ten minutes and come back to it?

acknowledge.acknowledge: The client asked for pricing first. Next time I'll check with you before I change the order, even when it's urgent.
acknowledge.defend: Honestly, the client changes things all the time. I can't promise anything.
acknowledge.attack: Maybe you should plan for changes instead of complaining about them.
acknowledge.withdraw: I don't know. Let's just get on with the agenda.
acknowledge.pause: Let me look at how we hand over changes. I'll come back to you this afternoon with a proposal.

defend.acknowledge: You're right, you redid work because of me. Next time I'll tell you the same day the client asks, before anything moves.
defend.defend: Nothing. It wasn't my decision, so I don't see what I could do differently.
defend.attack: You're making a big deal out of a few hours of work.
defend.withdraw: Can we not do this now? Next item.
defend.pause: I'm getting defensive. Give me ten minutes, then let's work out what I'll do differently.

attack.acknowledge: Yes. Sorry, that was unfair. I changed the plan without asking you, and you had to redo your part.
attack.defend: I wasn't attacking you. I was only stating facts.
attack.attack: Oh please. Even an intern would cope with a change of order.
attack.withdraw: Forget it. I'm not discussing this.
attack.pause: You're right. I need a few minutes to calm down. Can we pick this up at three?

withdraw.acknowledge: Yes. I changed the plan late and you had to redo work. Let's sort it out now.
withdraw.defend: There's nothing to resolve. The client decided, not me.
withdraw.attack: Why do you always make such a drama of everything?
withdraw.withdraw: No. I've said all I'm going to say.
withdraw.pause: Yes. Give me until after lunch and I'll come to your desk.

pause.acknowledge: Thanks for waiting. You're right, I changed the plan late. From now on I'll check with you first.
pause.defend: I've thought about it, and the client really forced my hand. There's nothing to fix.
pause.attack: I've thought about it, and I think you overreact to every change.
pause.withdraw: Actually, let's leave it. It's not worth it.
pause.pause: I need a bit longer. Can we finish this tomorrow at nine?

stageNotes.withdraw:withdraw: Michel turns to his screen and says nothing more in the meeting.
stageNotes.defend:withdraw: Michel says nothing for the rest of the meeting.

pauseNote: Ten minutes later, you're back with Michel.
unsure: It's unclear how Michel would take that. Rephrase it or choose a reply.
offScript: Michel is waiting for an answer about the plan.
